§6Lithium, Graphite & Asbestos

§aThree materials your reactors cannot function without.

§6Lithium§f (atomic 3):
Semi-rare alkali metal. §cExplodes if wet§f. Found in schist ore, nether quartz, meteorites.
Uses: §bLithium-Ion Batteries§f (with cobalt), §btritium breeding§f for fusion, thermonuclear warheads, custom nukes.

§6Graphite§f:
Crystalline carbon, the essential neutron moderator. Press lignite coke with flat stamp for ingots, or acidize coal blocks with hydrogen peroxide.
Uses: §bRBMK moderators and control rods§f, ZIRNOX reactor (16 ingots), Chicago Pile blocks, graphite electrodes for arc furnace, Watz fuel pellets.

§6Asbestos§f:
Rare silicate mineral. §cToxic when airborne§f, causes lung damage without protection. Found as underground ore or chrysotile cave walls.
Uses: §bInsulators§f (2 sheets = 16 insulators, very efficient), §basbestos concrete§f for RBMK columns, laboratory tiles, breeding reactor.

§ePS:§f Set up schist processing for lithium. Graphite from lignite coke is the easiest path. Asbestos, you only need modest amounts.
